title: A small tip for even slices
allegory: A policy is a spinner with one slice per move, learning widens the slices of moves that paid off, and the entropy bonus is a small tip for keeping the slices even, so one slice cannot swallow the wheel before the others have been tried.
map: a spinner with one slice per move
widening the slices of moves that paid off
how even the slices are: even is highest, one giant slice is zero
a small tip for keeping slices even
one slice swallowing the wheel too early
premature determinism: the policy stops exploring

chapters.name: Stuck on one move
chapters.note: it worked once, so now it's all I do

cap.1: Your agent found one move that worked early, and now it does nothing else. It never learns whether something better was one try away.
cap.2: Policy gradients sharpen the policy towards actions that paid off. Sharpen too fast and it goes deterministic before it has explored, then stops learning.
cap.3: Premature determinism: as π(a|s) nears one-hot, sampled trajectories stop covering alternatives, so gradient estimates carry no signal about them.

cap.1: Picture the policy as a spinner with a slice for each move. Learning widens the slices of moves that paid off. One slice can swallow the wheel too soon.
cap.2: π(a|s) gives each action a probability. Each update shifts probability towards actions with positive advantage, and with noisy early returns it can over-commit.
cap.3: Early policy-gradient estimates are high-variance; one lucky advantage estimate can push a logit up until the softmax saturates and its gradient vanishes.

cap.1: Entropy scores how even the slices are: highest when all are equal, zero when one slice is the whole wheel. The bonus pays a little for evenness.
cap.2: H(π) = −Σ π log π is the average surprise of the policy's own choices. Add ent_coef × H to the objective and the policy cannot sharpen quite so fast.
cap.3: Uniform over n actions gives log n; deterministic gives 0. PPO's objective is clipped surrogate − value loss + ent_coef·H, with ent_coef = 0.01 in ARENA.

cap.1: Two moves: slide from 50/50 towards all-in on one. Evenness is highest in the middle and drops to zero at the edges, fastest right at the end.
cap.2: Binary entropy peaks at log 2 ≈ 0.69 nats for a 50/50 policy and falls to 0 as one action takes everything. The slope steepens near the edges.
cap.3: dH/dp = log((1−p)/p), unbounded as p → 0 or 1: the bonus pushes back hardest exactly where the policy is about to go deterministic.

chapters.name: Tip, not salary
chapters.verdict: A small tip, not a salary: 0.01 in ARENA's PPO.

cap.1: Tip too little and the spinner collapses early. Tip too much and the agent keeps spinning evenly, ignoring what actually pays. Keep it small.
cap.2: Too small an ent_coef lets the policy collapse early; too large keeps it near random so returns stop improving. ARENA's PPO uses 0.01. Mind the sign in your loss.
cap.3: Entropy regularisation biases the optimum towards stochastic policies, trading return for randomness. Added to an objective you maximise, it is subtracted from a loss you minimise.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: The same term in PPO and in RLHF
Log entropy: a crash to zero means exploring stopped
Sampling temperature: a related dial on randomness

cap.1: The same small tip turns up in PPO and in the RL used to fine-tune chatbots. When training stalls, check how fast the policy's entropy fell.
cap.2: PPO and RLHF keep the entropy term unchanged. Logging the policy's entropy is a cheap early warning: a crash towards zero means exploration has stopped.
cap.3: For a language policy, entropy is diversity of generations. Tracking it beside reward and KL shows whether fine-tuning is narrowing the model more than you intended.

coda.title: Load the spinner. Which sharpness scores best once evenness earns a tip?

params.label: sharpness: how loaded the spinner is

readouts.label: entropy (even = 1.386)
readouts.f: round(-1000 * sum(softmax([1, 0.8, 0.5, 0].map(r => beta * r)).map(p => p > 0 ? p * log(p) : 0))) / 1000

caption.1: Slide sharpness to make 'reward + tip × entropy' as big as you can. With a small tip the best spinner is heavily loaded; with a big tip it stays more even.
caption.2: The bonus changes what 'best' means: the winning policy is no longer all-in on one move. Its best sharpness is exactly 1 / ent_coef.
caption.3: argmax_π E_π[R] + τH(π) = softmax(R/τ): entropy regularisation makes the optimum a Boltzmann policy at temperature τ, never deterministic for τ > 0.

where_else: PPO's full objective, and the RL stage of RLHF
Sampling temperature: dialling the randomness of a language model's next token
Maximum-entropy RL such as soft actor-critic, where the entropy term is central
Label smoothing: stopping a classifier from becoming certain too fast

hamming.what: A small reward for keeping a policy's choices spread out, measured by its entropy −Σ π log π.
hamming.when: Whenever a policy-gradient agent risks going deterministic before it has explored: REINFORCE, PPO, RLHF.
hamming.why: A policy that commits too early stops generating the experience it would need to discover it was wrong.

object.title: The tipping bowl
object.subtitle: Each spot is one way to load a three-slice spinner; depth is reward plus the evenness tip.
object.f: -(dot(softmax([x, y, 0]), [1, 0.5, 0]) - tau * sum(softmax([x, y, 0]).map(p => p * log(p))))

cap.1: Each spot on the floor is one way of loading a three-slice spinner. Depth is how good that loading is: reward plus the evenness tip.
cap.2: x, y = logits of moves A and B (C fixed at 0). Height = −(expected reward + τ·entropy), with rewards 1, 0.5 and 0.
cap.3: −J(θ) for a softmax policy over three actions, rewards (1, 0.5, 0), entropy weight τ.

cap.1: The lowest spot is not at the edge: with a tip, the best spinner still gives the weaker moves a sliver.
cap.2: The optimum sits at logits (1/τ, 0.5/τ): a softmax policy, not a one-hot one.
cap.3: The stationary point is at logits R/τ up to a shift, i.e. the Boltzmann policy softmax(R/τ).

cap.1: Shrink the tip and the lowest spot runs off towards the edge: the best spinner is almost all one slice.
cap.2: As ent_coef → 0 the optimum approaches the deterministic greedy policy.
cap.3: τ → 0 recovers the argmax policy; the regularised optimum converges to the unregularised one.

cap.1: Raise the tip and the best spinner stays much more even. Too much, and it barely prefers the best move at all.
cap.2: A large ent_coef keeps the policy near random and gives up reward to do it.
cap.3: Large τ flattens softmax(R/τ) towards uniform: return is traded for entropy.

cap.1: Drop the bead and watch it settle where reward and evenness balance. That is what the tip does during training.
cap.2: Gradient steps on the regularised objective settle at the softmax optimum instead of running to the edge.
cap.3: Ascent on J converges to the interior optimum; without τ it drifts towards the boundary, where softmax gradients vanish.

predict.q: A four-move policy puts all its probability on one move. What is its entropy?
predict.why: Entropy is zero for a deterministic policy and largest, log 4, when all four moves are equally likely.

predict.q: Your agent's entropy crashed to near zero early and returns stopped improving. What might help?

options.t: A larger entropy coefficient, so it keeps exploring

predict.why: The policy went deterministic before it had explored; the entropy bonus pushes back against exactly that.

predict.q: With an entropy bonus, what does the best possible policy look like?

options.t: Mostly the best move, but never all of it

predict.why: Maximising reward plus τ times entropy gives softmax(R/τ): tilted towards the best move, never fully deterministic.

object.where: Anywhere certainty must be rationed: RL exploration, sampling temperature, label smoothing.
